reason: Both galvanize steel and act as intermediate metal processors, so the offering overlaps. AZZ is mainly a hot-dip galvanizer of customer-fabricated steel for infrastructure and a coil coater. Worthington Steel buys coil and processes it (pickling, slitting, blanking, galvanizing, laminations, tailor welded blanks) for automotive, appliance and construction customers. Customers and end markets overlap only in part (appliance, construction), and the automotive-driven steel processing model differs. Overlap is real but not on both product and customers.

primary_services.reason: Both offer galvanizing; AZZ adds coil coating and surface technologies, while Worthington adds pickling, slitting, blanking and laminations.

end_markets.reason: AZZ leans toward infrastructure and construction. Worthington leans toward automotive, with appliance and construction also served. The overlap is partial.

business_model.reason: Both are processors that add value to steel. AZZ coats steel supplied by customers, while Worthington is an intermediate processor of carbon flat-rolled steel.

value_chain_position.reason: Both sit in the middle of the metal chain as processors or coaters, serving different downstream users.
